headline: Charlotte shops by car, and the Jumpman is its luxury badge
summary: Charlotte is a Piedmont car town that shops out in the sprawl, at Concord Mills, SouthPark and Charlotte Premium Outlets. The fan base spans NC and York and Lancaster counties in SC. Spending peaks at Black Friday, Christmas and the CIAA Tournament, on top of 1990s Hornets nostalgia that never left. A wide income gap calls for a clear good-better-best price ladder.

insights.title: The Jordan Brand franchise, and fans know it
insights.detail: The Hornets wear the Jumpman on their uniforms. Michael Jordan owned the team for over a decade and sold the majority stake in 2023. Jordan equity and Hornets equity are fused here in a way no other market matches, so fans buy teal-and-purple Jordan product as team product.
insights.implication: Plan Hornets apparel and Jordan Brand drops as one calendar. A Hornets collection without a Jumpman story, or a Jordan drop with no teal, will feel half-built here.

insights.title: 1988-1997 nostalgia outsells the present
insights.detail: The original Hornets run is the brand's emotional peak: Muggsy Bogues, Larry Johnson, Alonzo Mourning, Dell Curry, Glen Rice and the Alexander Julian pinstripes. The Hornets name came back to the franchise in 2014. Classic-teal throwbacks and "Buzz City" graphics sell across age groups, well beyond older fans.
insights.implication: Reissue-style product is the safe fall volume play: pinstripe, Hugo, original wordmark colorways. Layer current-roster product on top instead of leading with it.

insights.title: A state line cuts through the shopper base
insights.detail: North Carolina has no sales-tax holiday. It ended its back-to-school weekend years ago, and Mecklenburg County's combined rate is roughly 7.25 percent. South Carolina next door runs an early-August tax-free weekend. Fans in Fort Mill, Rock Hill and Lancaster County shop on both sides, as does Concord Mills' regional draw.
insights.implication: Don't market a tax-free promise in NC. Compete with early-August SC timing, outlet events and free-shipping thresholds.

insights.title: Mega-malls and outlets, not a flagship street
insights.detail: Concord Mills is one of the most-visited retail destinations in the Carolinas. SouthPark Mall is the upscale anchor. Charlotte Premium Outlets pulls traffic from the I-85 and I-77 corridors. The arena team store handles gameday, but everyday buying is spread across the suburbs.
insights.implication: Wholesale, outlet-grade placement and pop-ups at Spectrum Center will reach more fans than one Uptown store. Keep outlet price tiers distinct from full-price drops.

insights.title: Mild weather, short real winter
insights.detail: Summers are hot and humid, and spring and fall run long and pleasant. Winter cold comes in bursts, and the odd ice or snow event creates sudden demand for hoodies and fleece. Layering pieces and warm-ups outsell parkas.
insights.implication: Lead cold-weather product with mid-weight fleece, shell jackets and shooting shirts in teal and purple. Keep heavy outerwear to a small run tied to December and January.

insights.title: Event spikes beat a flat calendar
insights.detail: The CIAA Tournament filled Uptown with HBCU fans and apparel buyers in late February or early March from 2006 to 2020. It now plays in Baltimore. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte Motor Speedway on Memorial Day weekend brings a different race-fan spend. Carolina Panthers home games share the Uptown footprint.
insights.implication: Treat the CIAA-week legacy as a February moment, with HBCU-respectful product partnerships. Time Hornets and Jordan drops to dodge the Panthers and speedway weekends, or to ride them on purpose.

insights.title: Income spread demands a price ladder
insights.detail: Charlotte is a banking and finance hub, with Bank of America and Truist headquarters and a large Wells Fargo presence. Its southern suburbs are affluent, while the West Side and east Charlotte are far more price-sensitive. Kids' and youth jerseys sell steadily because of school and rec-league play.
insights.implication: Set a clear ladder: knock-off-proof Swingman at mid price, premium Authentic for the finance-and-suburb buyer, and accessible youth and graphic tees for the wider base.

places.name: Spectrum Center
places.why: Hornets home arena, team store and CIAA Tournament venue. It is the main gameday retail and pop-up spot.

places.name: Concord Mills
places.why: Huge outlet-style mall that draws Carolinas and regional visitors, good for family and tourist buying.

places.name: SouthPark Mall
places.why: The upscale retail anchor, serving affluent south Charlotte shoppers.

places.name: Charlotte Premium Outlets
places.why: Outlet traffic from across the I-85 and I-77 corridors and into South Carolina.

places.name: Charlotte Motor Speedway
places.why: The Memorial Day weekend Coca-Cola 600 and other race weekends bring a major regional shopper moment.

places.name: Carowinds
places.why: A literal state-line attraction that shows how NC and SC shoppers overlap.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.role: Hall of Famer, Jordan Brand founder, former Hornets owner
people.why: Anchors the Jumpman-on-Hornets link that shapes how Charlotte fans see premium product.

people.name: Muggsy Bogues
people.role: Original Hornets point guard, Charlotte resident
people.why: Beloved ambassador of the 1990s era, and a name that works on throwback graphics.

people.name: Dell Curry
people.role: Hornets all-time great and team broadcaster
people.why: Ties the old Hornets to the current game and to Stephen and Seth Curry.

people.name: Alexander Julian
people.role: Fashion designer of the original Hornets uniforms
people.why: His pinstripe teal-and-purple look is a North Carolina design heritage story.

people.name: Brandon Miller
people.role: Hornets forward, lead scorer of the post-LaMelo era
people.why: Face of the current roster for youth jersey demand.

people.name: Kon Knueppel
people.why: A rising name for the new jersey cycle, likely to draw youth and Swingman interest.

moments.name: Opening Cup Night and group play
moments.why: The Hornets sit in East Group C with Boston, Atlanta, Chicago and Washington, a built-in autumn merchandising story.

moments.name: Black Friday and holiday gifting
moments.why: The biggest buy window for jerseys, hoodies and youth gifts in the metro.

moments.name: Presidents' Day game vs. Minnesota
moments.why: LaMelo Ball's first return to Charlotte as a Timberwolf. The emotional storyline can move collector and commemorative product.

moments.name: CIAA Tournament
moments.why: A multi-day Uptown apparel and culture event centered on HBCU fans through 2020. It now plays in Baltimore, so treat it as legacy.

moments.name: Coca-Cola 600 weekend
moments.why: NASCAR spending brings out-of-town buyers to the metro, though it falls outside the Hornets season.

moments.name: South Carolina tax-free weekend
moments.why: Cross-border back-to-school shopping that pulls Charlotte-area buyers into SC retail.

moments.name: Charlotte Pride
moments.why: A large Uptown weekend where inclusive apparel and Hornets-brand partnerships can show up.

productHooks: Throwback pinstripe capsule: Alexander Julian-inspired teal and purple stripe jerseys, shorts and fleece, timed for October through Black Friday.
Jordan Brand x Hornets holiday collection that pairs Jumpman with classic Hornets teal on hoodies, warm-ups and youth sets.
Feb 15, 2027 return-night tee built around the new core and the city. No Ball likeness, and check rights before any player graphic.
February HBCU-legacy capsule made with HBCU-credited designers and licensed school partners for the late-winter Uptown moment.
Tiered jersey ladder: Authentic for the finance-and-suburbs buyer, Swingman for the core, and youth and kids' sizes for school and rec-league buyers.
watchouts: Jordan Brand imagery and any Hornets-plus-Jordan co-branding need Jordan Brand approval. The original Hornets logos and Hugo are team IP.
CIAA and HBCU marks are licensed. Engage the conference, the schools and Black Charlotte designers, and credit and pay them.
Don't market a tax-free weekend in NC. The state has none, and SC rules change.
Player-likeness product after the LaMelo trade carries rights and sentiment risk. Check licensing and fan reaction before leaning on any single name.

Easter and spring family spending, with the Play-In window in mid April.

Draft and free agency news. Summer heat shifts buying to shorts and tees.

channels.role: Concord Mills, SouthPark and Charlotte Premium Outlets are the dominant everyday channels.
Spectrum Center is the gameday and tourist capture point, strongest on opening night and special-event games.
Nike.com, NBA Store and Fanatics serve Carolinas fans who don't live near Uptown.

channels.channel: Social commerce and Jordan Brand drops
channels.role: SNKRS-style drops and Jordan Brand content drive hype buyers, especially younger, sneaker-focused fans.
Throwback Hornets jerseys carry a strong secondary market, and vintage 1990s originals are collectible.

extra.priceProfile: Mixed. The finance-and-professional suburbs (SouthPark, Ballantyne, Lake Norman, Fort Mill) can absorb premium Authentic and Jordan Brand pricing. The wider Carolinas base is more price-aware and responds to outlet tiers, bundles and youth value. Tier product so a clear entry point sits below the premium line.
extra.jerseyBehavior: Swingman is the core jersey, and youth and kids' sizes are the steady volume driver. Authentic skews to adult collectors and the finance-and-suburbs buyer. Throwback Hornets teal and pinstripe jerseys outsell most current-player jerseys in the metro. Counterfeit and resale activity makes licensed throwbacks a safe, differentiated play.
